chunks: He, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, also disliked shikal in horses.
It means that three standing legs of a horse have anklets and that one is free.

It stems from shikal, that which a horse is being decorated with. It was likened to it because shikal is only performed in three standing legs while the three are free and one has anklets. Shikal is not performed except in the foot, and it is not performed to a hand.

key_terms.الشِّكَالُ: A specific type of decoration or marking on horses, typically involving three legs.
key_terms.مُحْجَلَةً: Adorned or marked (specifically with a specific dye or mark on the legs).
key_terms.مُطْلَقَةً: Free, unmarked, or left as is.

ai.seo_question: What is the definition and ruling of Shikal in horses according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq clarifies that 'shikal' refers to a specific aesthetic practice where three of a horse's legs are adorned (hijala) while the fourth remains natural, a term derived from the resemblance to the leg's structure. This ruling is situated within the broader context of pre-Islamic and early Islamic commercial customs, where such decorative distinctions were used to identify or enhance the value of livestock for sale. The distinction between 'rajul' (leg) and 'yad' (arm/hand) underscores the precise anatomical application of this tradition in equine trade.
